chat.modeDesc.auto-safe: Default. Almost everything is approved right away, but the agent still asks before force-deleting files, rewriting git history, pushing or publishing, running scripts from the internet, using admin rights, touching secret files (.env, keys), or opening folders outside the project.
chat.risk.outside: Asked because it accesses a folder outside the project.
chat.risk.loop: Asked because the agent keeps repeating the same action.
chat.risk.secret: Asked because it touches a secret file (.env, keys, credentials, or .git internals).
chat.risk.delete: Asked because it force-deletes or recursively deletes files.
chat.risk.git-history: Asked because it can discard changes or rewrite git history.
chat.risk.publish: Asked because it sends something out (push, publish, release, merge).
chat.risk.remote-script: Asked because it runs a script from the internet.
chat.risk.system: Asked because it uses admin rights or changes the system or processes.
chat.risk.global-install: Asked because it installs or removes system-wide packages.
chat.risk.unknown: Asked because Zandor does not recognize this permission type yet.
chat.modeDesc.ask: The agent stops and asks for your approval whenever it wants to change files, run commands, fetch web pages, or open folders outside the project.
chat.modeDesc.auto-edit: File edits are approved right away. Terminal commands, web access, and other permissions still wait for your approval.
chat.modeDesc.auto-all: Every permission request is approved right away, including terminal commands. The agent works without pausing — use it only in folders you trust.

onb.thanks.tip: Press Ctrl+K anytime to open the command palette, including to reopen this tour.
onb.mem.what: Memory stores facts about you and your projects (name, preferences, decisions) and gives them to the agent in every conversation.
onb.mem.auto.pro: The agent knows you and the project context without repeating it.
onb.mem.auto.con: Uses a few extra tokens per turn; wrong facts may be kept until you delete them.
onb.mem.manual.pro: Full control: only the projects you pick are remembered.
onb.mem.manual.con: You must turn it on yourself; new sessions remember nothing until then.
onb.mem.off.con: Context and preferences must be explained again every session.
onb.skill.what: The skill creator spots repeated workflows and proposes them as skills (reusable instructions). Proposals always wait for your approval.
onb.skill.auto.pro: Zandor gets more capable over time without you writing skills.
onb.skill.auto.con: Occasionally proposes things you don't need to review; a few extra tokens.
onb.skill.manual.pro: Proposals only appear in projects you choose.
onb.skill.off.pro: No interruptions and no extra tokens.
onb.skill.off.con: Skills only grow when you write them yourself.
onb.import.step1: 1. Copy this prompt into the AI you usually use
onb.import.prompt:
I am moving to a new AI assistant called Zandor. Write down everything you remember or know about me from our conversations: identity, work, projects, preferred answer style, tools I use, and work habits.

Format rules (required):
- One fact per line, starting with "- ", in the format key: value
- Use these keys when relevant: name, nickname, occupation, company, location, time zone, language, answer style, expertise, tools, projects, interests, avoid
- You may add other short keys if needed
- Only write what you actually know, do not guess
- Do not include passwords, API keys, card numbers, or other sensitive data
- Reply only with that list inside a single code block, with no explanation
onb.import.copied: Prompt copied. Paste it into ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or another AI.
onb.import.step2: 2. Paste the reply here (from one or more AIs)
onb.import.secrets: {n} lines dropped because they look like secrets (keys/tokens).
onb.import.conflictsHint: This has only one correct answer, but different AIs answered differently. Zandor doesn't guess — pick the right one or write your own.
onb.import.customHint: If none is right, enter the correct value.
onb.import.listsHint: These values complement each other, so all are kept. Uncheck the wrong ones, or add your own.
onb.import.preview: What will be saved to global memory
onb.import.memOff: Note: default memory is off, so these facts are only used in projects/sessions where you turn memory on.
onb.import.webOnly: Outside the desktop app memory is only a preview and isn't read by the engine.
onb.import.optional: This step is optional; skip it with the Next button.

remote.intro: Connect projects to an opencode engine already running on another machine (VPS, another computer). Zandor does not install or run the engine there: start it yourself with `opencode serve` and OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD. URLs to other machines must be HTTPS; without HTTPS use an SSH tunnel (ssh -L 4096:127.0.0.1:4096 server) and enter http://127.0.0.1:4096. Models, providers, and Chat still use the local engine; documents in Panel 3 are read from this computer's disk.

sugg.summarize-text.label: Summarize text

auto.title: Scheduled Automation
auto.openOnly: Tasks only run while Zandor is open. Tasks missed while the app was closed run once when it is opened again.
auto.noAutoApprove: Tasks never approve permissions on their own: when the agent needs permission (file edits, shell commands, …) the session waits for you and you get a notification.
auto.notifOff: System notifications are not allowed yet.
auto.notifUnavailable: System notifications are unavailable here; messages appear inside the app only.
auto.deleteBody: The schedule is removed. Sessions already created are kept.
auto.name: Task name
auto.promptHint: Sent to the agent every time the task runs, in a new session.
auto.notif.title: Zandor: {name}
auto.notif.needsPermission: Task {name} is waiting for your approval.
usage.warnSoon: The context window is nearly full. Consider compacting the history or starting a new session.
usage.warnHigh: The context window is almost exhausted; the next reply may fail or be truncated.
usage.quotaNote: Provider quotas/rate limits are not exposed by the engine, so they are not shown here.
rich.noImageClipboard: Image clipboard is not supported here
link.openZandorDesktop: Open in Zandor browser (desktop app only)
doc.mermaidStreaming: The diagram will render once the reply is complete.
queue.title: Queued messages ({n})
queue.hint: Sent in order after the agent finishes.
q.title: Question from the agent
q.malformed: The agent sent a question that couldn't be read. Skip it so the agent can continue.
q.multiHint: You can pick more than one.
todo.title: Agent plan: {done} of {total} steps done
todo.heading: Plan
ow.intro: Connect your OpenWork Cloud account. Zandor uses that account's AI Gateway as a provider (OpenAI-compatible models). You can add more than one account.
ow.step1: 1. Open the OpenWork page in your browser and sign in.
ow.step2: 2. Make sure this code matches the one on the page, then approve:
ow.waiting: Waiting for approval… (code valid for {s} s)
ow.desktopOnly: Sign in with OpenWork is only available in the desktop app.
ow.privacy: The account token and gateway key are handled and stored in the keychain by the app; they are never shown or written to config files.
acc.title: Accounts
acc.label: Account name
acc.confirmBody: This account's key is removed from the keychain. Other accounts on this provider are unaffected.
acc.note: One active account is used by the engine; switch any time without re-entering the key.
acc.oauthNote: Browser login: the engine keeps only one login per provider. For several accounts, use API keys (Catalog tab).
voice.notDefault: Windows dictation uses the system default microphone, not {device}. Make {device} the default in Sound settings.
